headline: A windy, rainy front hits Friday, Saturday brings a mild lull, and a stronger windy system arrives Saturday night.
summary: A strong Pacific front moves in tonight, with rain spreading across western Washington early Friday morning and falling mostly during the day. The windiest areas are the coast, Whidbey and San Juan Islands, and the northern Interior (western Whatcom and Skagit counties), where winds of 20-30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph are possible. Wind Advisories are in effect there Friday: 1 AM to 1 PM on the Northern Washington Coast, 4 AM to 4 PM for the island and northern lowland areas, and 7 AM to 4 PM on the Grays Harbor County coast. Rain totals reach about one-half to three-quarters of an inch at most over the mountains and coast, and about one-tenth to one-quarter of an inch in most other lowlands. Snow levels start around 5,000-6,000 feet and rise to about 9,000 feet Friday afternoon, so high-elevation snow is not a big concern. Saturday is a relative lull with leftover clouds, a few showers, and highs in the 60s for most lowlands. Another front arrives Saturday night with a new round of strong winds. The coast, islands, and northern Interior will likely see advisory-level winds, and other places along Puget Sound might too, but it is too early to decide on alerts. Winds ease quickly Sunday, with most breezy conditions ending by mid-morning. After a brief break Sunday night into Monday, more rain arrives from Monday afternoon into Tuesday. Temperatures stay a few degrees above normal, with lows mostly in the mid 40s to around 50. The active pattern continues into at least the first half of next week. River flooding is not expected in the next seven days, but repeated rain will wet the soil and raise river flows, which could matter with later storms. Forecasters are fairly confident about Friday's winds, but less sure how far Saturday night's winds will reach. Computer models disagree about Wednesday, with one keeping systems offshore and another bringing rain at least to the Olympic Peninsula. Gale Warnings and other marine alerts are in effect, and the Grays Harbor Bar could see rough to severe conditions starting Friday.
changes: The evening update put more emphasis on Saturday night's system, saying advisory-level winds are likely in several areas and possibly along Puget Sound, and it added detail on Sunday's quick wind easing and a Monday-Tuesday rain return. The morning mention of a possible early arrival this evening and a roughly 20-foot swell on the coast was dropped.
